resources.string: Lets TVRelay detect when you select a movie or show recommendation on the launcher, so it can open it in the app you\'ve chosen in Settings instead.

TVRelay uses an Accessibility Service to detect when you click a movie or show recommendation on your TV's home screen. When it does, it sends only that title's text to a metadata service (TMDB by default, or TheTVDB - see Settings) to identify it, then shows a "Watch now" button for the app you've chosen in Settings - tapping it (and only tapping it) opens that title there, so an accidental click never jumps you into another app on its own.

Nothing else is read, collected, or sent anywhere. Every other click (apps, menus, anything that isn't a content recommendation) is left completely alone.

You can turn the service off at any time from this app's Settings.

Some recommendation cards - especially the \"Top picks for you\" row - don\'t include any readable title in the click TVRelay receives. When this is on, TVRelay uses Android\'s screen-recording permission to capture what\'s on screen. Android will show a persistent \"recording/casting\" indicator.

Fire TV's home screen doesn't let TVRelay detect a clicked recommendation the way Google TV does. Instead, Fire TV mode notices when you open a recommendation and reads its title off the screen using on-device text recognition, then opens it in your chosen app.

It needs two one-time permissions: Usage access (to notice when you open a recommendation) and Screen recording (to read the title - nothing ever leaves the device). While it's active, Android shows a persistent recording indicator, which it can't hide.

Because screen-recording permission is cleared on a reboot, you'll need to activate Fire TV mode again after restarting the device.

If you sideloaded this app and the Accessibility toggle switches itself back off right after you enable it: that's Android's "Restricted settings" protection for apps not installed from an app store, not a bug. Many Google TV/Android TV devices don't have an "Allow restricted setting" option anywhere in Settings to clear this - if yours does, it's on this app's system App info screen, in the overflow/three-dot menu. If not (or you'd rather skip hunting for it), connect over ADB - or use the atvTools app (free, Google Play) from your phone if you don't have a computer handy - and run:

adb shell appops set com.hmartinez94.tvrelay ACCESS_RESTRICTED_SETTINGS allow
adb shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.hmartinez94.tvrelay/com.hmartinez94.tvrelay.TvRelayAccessibilityService
adb shell settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1

(The last command replaces the whole list - separate services with a colon if you already use another one, like TalkBack.)
